title: Antoni Augustyn Deboli to King Stanisław August, cipher despatches from St Petersburg, 1790 (AGAD Zbiór Popielów 4; catalogue 419)

documents.shelfmark: AGAD Warszawa, Zbiór Popielów (zesp. 12), sygn. 4, k. 1-350 (109 despatches)

plaintext.source: The cabinet's decipherments, filed apart: ZbPop 417 k. 353-386 (2 Jan - 2 Feb 1790) and ZbPop 420 (5 Feb - 31 Dec 1790); paired by date in pairs.tsv.

transcription.source: AGAD scans on agadd2.home.net.pl, album 4 (images 0002 and 0049).
transcription.notes: Only the opening six lines of two despatches (2 Jan, 9 Feb) were transcribed, for the alignment test; the measured count is that sample, not the volume (about 400 images of code groups). 0/8 and 6/b look alike in this hand.

system.summary: A Polish numerical code of syllables and words, groups of 1-4 digits (to about 2160) with subscript a/b/c variants, under a clear French heading.

diacritics.note: Subscript letters a, b, c under some groups.

system.notes: Three equivalences checked against the decipherments: 1559 = w, 1092 = po-, 606 = z. Probably the 'Cyfra polska' sent to Deboli on 8 III 1783 (ZbPop 444, not online); not verified.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary cabinet decipherments in AGAD Zbiór Popielów 417 (k. 353-386) and 420; used by Rolnik 2025 without linking them to ZbPop 4.

conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue task; no other input.
tools: pdf.js in the built-in browser (RCIN edition)

solution.what: Fetched the ZbPop 4 letter list and scans; viewed k. 2-4: code groups only, French heading, no interlinear decipherment.
Looked for the keys ZbPop 444, 451, 453, 454 and the deciphered register ZbPop 320 on agadd2 and AGAD's inventories.
Contact sheets of all scanned cipher volumes (ZbPop 428, 17, 4, 5, 416) to look for decipherment pages among the ciphers.

Zielinska & Danilczyk, Deboli 1782 (IH PAN 2017), introduction: the cabinet kept decipherments of Deboli's despatches (AKP 265). Rolnik 2025 cites the 1790-92 texts in ZbPop 415/420/421 as ciphered correspondence.
ZbPop 420 holds the decipherments of ZbPop 4: matched AGAD's two letter lists by date; 99 of 109 despatches in ZbPop 420, the other 10 at the end of ZbPop 417.
Opening six lines of the 2 Jan and 9 Feb despatches (transcription_sample.md).

Aligned the transcribed groups with the decipherments' opening words: 1559 = w and 1092 = po- in both pairs, 606 = z twice in 9 Feb; headings and receipt dates identical; image counts correlate r = 0.69.
Checked one of the 17 copies AGAD lists as addressed to Kicinski (16 July 1790): headed 'Sire!' with the cipher's receipt date, so the King's copy.

outcome.method_basis: Every one of the 109 cipher despatches has a contemporary cabinet decipherment in ZbPop 417 or 420, matched by date and heading and checked by code-group alignment on two pairs.
outcome.notes: Catalogue 419 closed: deciphered at the time. Added here: the 109 cipher/decipherment pairs (pairs.tsv), three code equivalences, and the inventory's wrong addressee on the Kicinski items. Code not rebuilt.

credits.note: Stanisław August's cabinet decipherments, AGAD Zbiór Popielów 417 k. 353-386 and 420
cites the ZbPop 420 texts as Deboli's ciphered despatches, which led to the pairing
